info.desc: The Next Day is the twenty-fourth studio album by David Bowie. The album was announced on January 8th, 2013, Bowie's sixty-sixth birthday. It is Bowie's first album of new material in ten years, since 2003's Reality, and surprised fans and media who believed he had retired. The Next Day Extra, an additional disc featuring four more tracks, and remixes of songs from the original album, was released eight months later in November. The Next Day was met with critical acclaim, and earned Bowie his first number-one album in the UK since 1993's Black Tie White Noise. The cover art for .

podcast.body: Recorded secretly between 2011 and 2012, featuring 29 brand new songs, this album was released on March 8, 2013, two months after the surprise single "Where Are We Now?". Its artwork was a cheeky takeoff of his 1977 *Heroes* album cover. It debuted at number one in the UK and number two in both the US and Canada. Critics considered it his best work since *Scary Monsters* (1980) and it was nominated for two Grammys, preceding Beyoncé as the first of a series of surprise albums released by superstar acts in the 2010s. "The greatest trick Bowie ever pulled was convincing the world he'd retired."

podcast.body: This album was secretly recorded over two years in a studio near his New York apartment, marking Bowie's return to music after a period of retirement from live performances. It was released as a "gift to fans" without any accompanying performances. "Bowie had been well enough to secretly record an album and title the next day in 2013, something that took two years to make it a nearby studio that was within walking distance of his apartment."

podcast.body: This album was secretly written and recorded over a period of two years, with no one involved leaking information. Its existence was announced on Bowie's 66th birthday, January 8th, 2013, along with a new song. The ability to record such an album in total secrecy during the internet age was considered a "miracle," attributed to the loyalty of his associates and Bowie's low-key life in New York. "The first the world heard of this record was on January 8th, 2013, Bowie 66th birthday. All of a sudden, there was a new song and the announcement of a new album called The Next Day."

podcast.body: This album, secretly recorded with producer Tony Visconti for over a year, was abruptly announced on Bowie's 66th birthday, January 8th, 2013, effectively ending his decade-long unofficial retirement. Despite the lead single's somber tone, the album was largely uptempo and rocking, though moody in its lyrics. It debuted at number one in the UK and a surprising number two on the Billboard 200 in the US, becoming his highest charting LP in America to date, though it was blocked from the top spot by a new Bon Jovi album. "And he announced the arrival of a new album two months later, which would be called the next day."
